title: Causal and final connectors
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal/Hide answer shows reference + speaker

exercises.english: I stayed at home because my daughter is ill.
exercises.german: Ich blieb zu Hause, weil meine Tochter krank ist.
exercises.why: weil-clause in second position after the main clause; conjugated ist goes to the very end, which also marks it as the subordinate clause.

exercises.english: We could not enter because the door was locked.
exercises.german: Wir konnten nicht eintreten, weil die Tür verschlossen war.
exercises.why: war is a conjugated auxiliary and therefore joins the verb cluster at the clause end after verschlossen.

exercises.english: Because the meeting was cancelled, I am working from home today.
exercises.german: Weil die Besprechung abgesagt wurde, arbeite ich heute von zu Hause.
exercises.why: weil may also open the sentence; only the verb of the main clause (arbeite) then takes position II.

exercises.english: She was late because she missed the last bus.
exercises.german: Sie kam zu spät, weil sie den letzten Bus verpasst hatte.
exercises.why: Perfect-plus in the weil-clause: hatte at the end carries the main clause tense (kam → hatte verpasst).

exercises.english: I don't trust the report because the figures contradict each other.
exercises.german: Ich vertraue dem Bericht nicht, weil die Zahlen einander widersprechen.
exercises.why: widersprechen is a strong verb, so the separated prefix widersprechen lands last after its object.

exercises.english: The project failed because nobody took responsibility.
exercises.german: Das Projekt scheiterte, weil niemand die Verantwortung übernommen hat.
exercises.why: Separable prefix übernommen stays in the verb cluster at the end; negation sits in the main clause before the verb.

exercises.english: I like this city less because rents have doubled.
exercises.german: Ich mag diese Stadt weniger, weil die Mieten sich verdoppelt haben.
exercises.why: Reflexive sich plus separable prefix verdoppelt: the reflexive pronoun precedes the prefix, haben closes the clause.

exercises.english: I can't sleep tonight because the neighbours are making noise again.
exercises.german: Ich kann heute Nacht nicht schlafen, weil die Nachbarn schon wieder Lärm machen.
exercises.why: The weil-clause carries a present tense that refers to the same now as the main clause.

exercises.english: He apologised because he had not noticed the sign.
exercises.german: Er entschuldigte sich, weil er das Schild nicht bemerkt hatte.
exercises.why: modal-like perfect with bemerkt: negation and the participle precede the final had.

exercises.english: We changed our plans because the weather forecast was bad.
exercises.german: Wir haben unsere Pläne geändert, weil die Wetterprognose schlecht war.
exercises.why: Main clause in perfect with a separable prefix (geändert), weil-clause in preterite with war.

exercises.english: I was surprised because she knew my new address.
exercises.german: Ich war überrascht, weil sie meine neue Adresse kannte.
exercises.why: kannte is the preterite of kennen (weak verb), so it sits last in the clause as a finite form.

exercises.english: The app keeps crashing because the memory is full.
exercises.german: Die App stürzt ständig ab, weil der Speicher voll ist.
exercises.why: Two separable verbs: abstürzen in the main clause in position II, and the weil-clause keeps the finite verb last.

exercises.english: She didn't get the job because her CV was too short.
exercises.german: Sie bekam die Stelle nicht, weil ihr Lebenslauf zu kurz war.
exercises.why: zu + adjective (zu kurz) inside the subordinate clause; the whole predicate war is finite and goes last.

exercises.english: We eat out a lot because the kitchen is being renovated.
exercises.german: Wir essen oft aus, weil die Küche renoviert wird.
exercises.why: Passive in the weil-clause: wird is the finite auxiliary and moves in front of the participle, which is the last element.

exercises.english: He didn't answer because he had already left the meeting.
exercises.german: Er antwortete nicht, weil er die Besprechung schon verlassen hatte.
exercises.why: Verbs of motion with a prefix (verlassen) form the perfect with haben and put the participle before the final hatte.

exercises.english: I rarely cook because I spend a lot of time travelling.
exercises.german: Ich koche selten, weil ich viel unterwegs bin.
exercises.why: A non-standard-sounding but idiomatic contrast of two habits; the weil-clause verb bin is the last word.

exercises.english: The medicine helps because it reduces the inflammation.
exercises.german: Das Medikament hilft, weil es die Entzündung hemmt.
exercises.why: Strong verb hemmt with prefix object hemm-en: the prefixed stem goes last in the subordinate clause.

exercises.english: We had to cancel because nobody was available on Sunday.
exercises.german: Wir mussten absagen, weil am Sonntag niemand Zeit hatte.
exercises.why: mussten is the inflected form of müssen in the main clause; am Sonntag is the accusative time phrase.

exercises.english: I can't decide because both options have serious advantages.
exercises.german: Ich kann mich nicht entscheiden, weil beide Optionen große Vorteile haben.
exercises.why: Reflexive sich plus modal-like kann: the infinitive entscheiden follows immediately, the reflexive pronoun sits before it.

exercises.english: He left the company because he had been offered a better position.
exercises.german: Er verließ die Firma, weil man ihm eine bessere Stelle angeboten hatte.
exercises.why: Double accusative in the weil-clause (ihm … eine Stelle); the participle precedes the final finite hatte.

exercises.english: Since you are back, let's have dinner together.
exercises.german: Da du wieder da bist, lass uns zusammen essen.
exercises.why: da as a temporal causal at the start of the sentence; the imperative clause uses the position-II verb (lass).

exercises.english: I am tired because the shift was very long.
exercises.german: Ich bin müde, denn die Schicht war sehr lang.
exercises.why: denn stays in position II and is followed by the full verb cluster, which is the most frequent option in writing.

exercises.english: The office is closed because the owner is on holiday.
exercises.german: Das Büro ist geschlossen, da der Besitzer im Urlaub ist.
exercises.why: da as a causal connector in first position, explained by an ist-statement about the Besitzer.

exercises.english: The museum is closed, because the entrance is being rebuilt.
exercises.german: Das Museum ist geschlossen, da der Eingang umgebaut wird.
exercises.why: da with a passive subordinate clause; wird is the finite verb and the participle umgebaut follows it.

exercises.english: The prices have gone up, as suppliers have become more expensive.
exercises.german: Die Preise sind gestiegen, denn die Lieferanten sind teurer geworden.
exercises.why: Both clauses are main clauses, so the second one repeats the subject and its verb in position II.

exercises.english: Since the tickets are sold out, we'll watch it at home.
exercises.german: Da die Karten ausverkauft sind, sehen wir uns den Film zu Hause an.
exercises.why: separable verb ansehen: the prefix an goes to the end of the main clause, but the conjugated sehen stays in position II.

exercises.english: Nobody came, for nobody had been informed.
exercises.german: Niemand kam, denn niemand war informiert worden.
exercises.why: Participle construction with worden instead of geworden shows the passive (informiert worden).

exercises.english: Take a jacket, because it will be cold this evening.
exercises.german: Nimm eine Jacke mit, denn es wird heute Abend kalt.
exercises.why: The separable prefix mit leaves the verb stem in position II, with mit as the last element of the sentence.

exercises.english: She knows a lot about it, because she wrote her thesis on the topic.
exercises.german: Sie weiß viel darüber, denn sie hat ihre Abschlussarbeit dazu geschrieben.
exercises.why: dazu is the local adverb; the causal denn in position II plus the verb cluster follows the comma.

exercises.english: Since I still have time, I'll wait for you.
exercises.german: Da ich noch Zeit habe, warte ich auf dich.
exercises.why: The um-clause could also be a weil-clause; da presents the reason as a neutral circumstance.

exercises.english: I don't think he'll come, because he has to work late.
exercises.german: Ich glaube nicht, dass er kommt, denn er muss spät arbeiten.
exercises.why: A hybrid: the main content is a dass-clause, and the actual reason is added in position I with denn.

exercises.english: I don't think he'll come, for he has to work late.
exercises.german: Ich glaube nicht, dass er kommt, da er spät arbeiten muss.
exercises.why: Here da takes a modal clause; the modal verb with its infinitive goes to the end of the subordinate clause.

exercises.english: Since the road is blocked, we take the train.
exercises.german: Da die Straße gesperrt ist, nehmen wir den Zug.
exercises.why: unmittelbarer temporaler Kausalzusammenhang: the blocked road causes the current decision, which is what da typically signals.

exercises.english: I was surprised, for nobody had mentioned it.
exercises.german: Ich war überrascht, denn niemand hatte es erwähnt.
exercises.why: Perfect plus with a strong verb: erwähnen has no prefix, so the finite hatte is simply the last word.

exercises.english: Since I'm already here, I'll show you around.
exercises.german: Da ich schon hier bin, zeige ich dir alles.
exercises.why: The main-clause verb has to change to the present after the da-clause, because the situation is still ongoing.

exercises.english: The file is corrupt, probably because it was not saved properly.
exercises.german: Die Datei ist beschädigt, vermutlich weil sie nicht richtig gespeichert wurde.
exercises.why: The verb likely belongs to the main clause, so the real reason after weil is given as a parenthetical clause.

exercises.english: I'd rather stay in tonight, for I'm simply exhausted.
exercises.german: Ich bleibe heute lieber zu Hause, denn ich bin einfach völlig erschöpft.
exercises.why: Two main clauses; den replaces weil to keep the register of spoken German simple.

exercises.english: The train is cheaper, so we should take the train.
exercises.german: Der Zug ist billiger, da sollten wir den Zug nehmen.
exercises.why: da is very frequent after a statement as a reformulation; shoulden is a modal and keeps position II in the second clause.

exercises.english: I didn't go out, because I had to look after the dog.
exercises.german: Da ich auf den Hund aufpassen musste, bin ich nicht ausgegangen.
exercises.why: Modal past musste in the da-clause with the perfect; the main clause keeps the perfect aus-gegangen.

exercises.english: The teacher repeated the rule, for several students had not understood it.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin wiederholte die Regel, denn mehrere Schüler hatten sie nicht verstanden.
exercises.why: denn in position I links the two main clauses; the perfect cluster had … verstanden stays intact in the second clause.

exercises.english: I get up early to be on time for work.
exercises.german: Ich stehe früh auf, um pünktlich zur Arbeit zu sein.
exercises.why: same subject (ich) in both parts, and the um-clause is a zu-infinitive without a conjugated verb.

exercises.english: She saved money to buy a bicycle.
exercises.german: Sie sparte Geld, um ein Fahrrad zu kaufen.
exercises.why: The zu-infinitive keeps its separable verb (kaufen) at the end; the subject is not repeated.

exercises.english: We booked early to get cheaper flights.
exercises.german: Wir haben früh gebucht, um günstigere Flüge zu bekommen.
exercises.why: Main clause in perfect (haben … gebucht), purpose clause with a zu-infinitive and no modal verb.

exercises.english: I called him in order to ask about the date.
exercises.german: Ich rief ihn an, um das Datum zu erfragen.
exercises.why: The separable verb anrufen in the main clause puts its prefix an at the end; the purpose is a zu-infinitive with the same subject.

exercises.english: Write it down in order not to forget it.
exercises.german: Schreib es auf, um es nicht zu vergessen.
exercises.why: The verb of purpose is negated with nicht before the zu-infinitive; the subject of both clauses is du.

exercises.english: The app asks for your location to show nearby restaurants.
exercises.german: Die App fragt nach deinem Standort, um Restaurants in der Nähe anzuzeigen.
exercises.why: Technically a subjectless purpose clause, which is why the zu-infinitive is the only verb form in it.

exercises.english: He moved abroad to learn a new language.
exercises.german: Er zog ins Ausland, um eine neue Sprache zu lernen.
exercises.why: A verb of motion towards a place of residence is allowed with um ... zu; only the direction away would need damit.

exercises.english: I repeat myself to make sure you understand.
exercises.german: Ich wiederhole mich, um sicherzugehen, dass du mich verstehst.
exercises.why: A dass-clause with position II verb (verstehst) can follow inside an um ... zu clause.

exercises.english: She practises every day to improve her pronunciation.
exercises.german: Sie übt jeden Tag, um ihre Aussprache zu verbessern.
exercises.why: The purpose infinitive with a separable prefix verb; verbessern is the last word of the sentence.

exercises.english: I set my alarm early to catch the morning flight.
exercises.german: Ich stelle den Wecker früh, um den Frühflug zu erwischen.
exercises.why: Both clauses have the subject ich, which is why um ... zu is possible here and damit would be wrong.

exercises.english: I take the stairs to save money.
exercises.german: Ich nehme die Treppe, um Geld zu sparen.
exercises.why: sparen is an infinitive with zu, and the zu-infinitive block comes after the comma.

exercises.english: We ate early to be hungry enough for the concert.
exercises.german: Wir haben früh gegessen, um für das Konzert satt genug zu sein.
exercises.why: A purpose clause with a prefixed separable verb: sein is the last element, no finite verb anywhere.

exercises.english: He works part-time to finance his studies.
exercises.german: Er arbeitet nebenbei, um sein Studium zu finanzieren.
exercises.why: A modal verb is not allowed in an um ... zu clause, which is why the main clause is in the present indicative here.

exercises.english: I bought a second pair of glasses in order to have a spare.
exercises.german: Ich habe eine zweite Brille gekauft, um eine Reserve zu haben.
exercises.why: The infinitive-having construction zu haben expresses purpose; both parts share the subject ich.

exercises.english: He moved to a smaller flat in order to reduce the rent.
exercises.german: Er zog in eine kleinere Wohnung, um die Miete zu senken.
exercises.why: The verb of motion is fine here because it states a change of residence, not a movement away from the speaker; the purpose is a zu-infinitive with senken.

exercises.english: We invited them in order to discuss the plan in person.
exercises.german: Wir haben sie eingeladen, um den Plan persönlich zu besprechen.
exercises.why: The purpose clause names no new subject, so zu plus the infinitive besprechen closes the sentence.

exercises.english: She drinks coffee in order to stay awake.
exercises.german: Sie trinkt Kaffee, um wach zu bleiben.
exercises.why: The infinitive with zu is attached to a prefixed adjective; bleiben is the last word of the sentence.

exercises.english: I check my mailbox every morning in order to see new messages.
exercises.german: Ich sehe jeden Morgen in mein Postfach, um neue Nachrichten zu sehen.
exercises.why: Purpose again with a zu-infinitive; sehen is the last word of the sentence and no conjugated verb appears in the purpose clause.

exercises.english: He is learning Italian in order to travel in Italy without a translator.
exercises.german: Er lernt Italienisch, um ohne Dolmetscher durch Italien zu reisen.
exercises.why: A longer purpose clause with separable prefix reisen; zu reisen is the last element.

exercises.english: I speak slowly so that the students can follow along.
exercises.german: Ich spreche langsam, um den Lernenden das Mitschreiben zu erleichtern.
exercises.why: Here the purpose has a different object, but the subject stays ich, so um ... zu is still correct.

exercises.english: I'll call you so that you know the new address.
exercises.german: Ich rufe dich an, damit du die neue Adresse weißt.
exercises.why: damit introduces a clause with a new subject (du) and verb-last weißt, so the main subject ich is not repeated.

exercises.english: I'll send you the document so that you can print it out.
exercises.german: Ich schicke dir das Dokument, damit du es ausdrucken kannst.
exercises.why: Modal kannst with the infinitive goes to the end of the damit-clause, which damit allows and um ... zu does not.

exercises.english: I will leave early so that we don't miss the start.
exercises.german: Wir fahren früh ab, damit wir nicht den Anfang verpassen.
exercises.why: Negative purpose with damit uses nicht inside the clause; verpassen is the prefixed verb at the end.

exercises.english: She repeats the words so that the children remember them.
exercises.german: Sie wiederholt die Wörter, damit die Kinder sie behalten.
exercises.why: Different subjects (sie / die Kinder) make damit mandatory; um ... zu would wrongly imply one subject.

exercises.english: I shut the window so that the noise doesn't get in.
exercises.german: Ich mache das Fenster zu, damit der Lärm nicht reinkommt.
exercises.why: Separable verb zumachen in the main clause with the prefix at the end; the damit-clause uses the simple present reinkommt.

exercises.english: We booked a table so that we wouldn't have to wait.
exercises.german: Wir haben einen Tisch reserviert, damit wir nicht warten mussten.
exercises.why: A modal in the damit-clause goes last as a cluster: warten mussten.

exercises.english: The hotel is building a wall so that the guests feel safer.
exercises.german: Das Hotel baut eine Wand, damit sich die Gäste sicherer fühlen.
exercises.why: Reflexive sich inside the damit-clause stands after the subject, and the reflexive verb closes the clause.

exercises.english: He spoke slowly so that I could understand every word.
exercises.german: Er sprach langsam, damit ich jedes Wort verstehen konnte.
exercises.why: konnte is the preterite of können and stands last, the subject of the clause (ich) differs from er.

exercises.english: She locked the door so that nobody could get in.
exercises.german: Sie schloss die Tür ab, damit niemand hereinkommen konnte.
exercises.why: Separable abschließen in the main clause; the damit-clause expresses consequence-free purpose with a modal.

exercises.english: We set the alarm so that we don't miss the bus.
exercises.german: Wir stellen den Wecker, damit wir den Bus nicht verpassen.
exercises.why: A negative purpose: negation inside the damit-clause applies to verpassen, not to the whole sentence.

exercises.english: The teacher explained the rule again so that we would remember it.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin erklärte die Regel noch einmal, damit wir sie uns merken würden.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv II (würden) is a soft purpose form typical of damit-clauses in formal German.

exercises.english: Take a pen so that you can write it down.
exercises.german: Nimm einen Stift, damit du es aufschreiben kannst.
exercises.why: Imperative main clause plus a damit-clause with a modal verb; separable aufschreiben keeps its prefix in place.

exercises.english: I'll give you a pen so that you can sign the form.
exercises.german: Ich gebe dir einen Stift, damit du das Formular unterschreiben kannst.
exercises.why: Two different subjects (ich / du) and a modal verb in the clause, both typical reasons for using damit.

exercises.english: The city closed the road so that the event could take place safely.
exercises.german: Die Stadt sperrte die Straße, damit die Veranstaltung sicher stattfinden konnte.
exercises.why: Passive sense with a modal; konnte is the last element of the damit-clause.

exercises.english: I'll explain it once more so that there are no doubts.
exercises.german: Ich erkläre es noch einmal, damit keine Zweifel bleiben.
exercises.why: A damit-clause with a negated subject (keine Zweifel) — um ... zu is impossible with a new subject.

exercises.english: We agreed on a date so that the trip can be planned.
exercises.german: Wir haben ein Datum vereinbart, damit die Reise geplant werden kann.
exercises.why: A damit-clause with a passive and a modal; this construction would be impossible with um ... zu.

exercises.english: He arrived early so that he could find a seat.
exercises.german: Er kam früh, damit er einen Platz finden konnte.
exercises.why: The subordinate clause expresses a purpose directed at a past event, hence preterite konnte.

exercises.english: I put the key on the table so that you find it easily.
exercises.german: Ich lege den Schlüssel auf den Tisch, damit du ihn leicht findest.
exercises.why: Present-subjunctive-style purpose with a present indicative, referring to a still valid arrangement.

exercises.english: The company hired a coach so that everyone could attend the fair.
exercises.german: Die Firma stellte einen Bus, damit alle die Messe besuchen konnten.
exercises.why: Both verbs are strong and separable; in the clause the finite konnte follows the prefixed infinitive.

exercises.english: I'll explain the reason so that you can decide afterwards.
exercises.german: Ich erkläre den Grund, damit du danach entscheiden kannst.
exercises.why: A temporal adverb danach inside the clause; modal verb last, subject du instead of ich.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Be careful so that you don't slip.
exercises.german: Pass auf, um nicht auszurutschen.
exercises.why: A warning: um nicht ... zu prevents something undesirable; ausrutschen is the zu-infinitive at the end.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Lock the door so that no one comes in unnoticed.
exercises.german: Schließ die Tür ab, um nicht unbemerkt hereinzukommen.
exercises.why: Negative purpose with nicht placed directly in front of the zu-infinitive; the subject du is not repeated.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why did you switch off the computer? So that it can cool down.
exercises.german: Warum hast du den Computer ausgeschaltet? Damit er abkühlen kann.
exercises.why: Nachfrage plus Antwort mit damit: der Infinitiv steht im Nebensatz am Ende und der Artikel bleibt im Vorfeld.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Put the milk back in the fridge so that it doesn't spoil.
exercises.german: Stell die Milch zurück in den Kühlschrank, um nicht zu verderben.
exercises.why: A negative purpose with a zu-infinitive of verderben; the subject is the same, so um ... zu fits.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why are you taking a taxi? To avoid waiting for the bus.
exercises.german: Wieso nimmst du ein Taxi? Um nicht auf den Bus warten zu müssen.
exercises.why: In this elliptical answer the modal appears in the um nicht ... zu form, which is the normal colloquial pattern.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: She learned the vocabulary twice, and in addition she recorded it, in order to pass the test.
exercises.german: Sie lernte den Wortschatz zweimal, dazu um den Test zu bestehen, und nahm ihn auf.
exercises.why: dazu um ... zu adds a second purpose to the action already mentioned; um cannot stand alone here.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: He writes down every unknown word, and additionally he looks it up, in order to expand his vocabulary.
exercises.german: Er notiert jedes unbekannte Wort, dazu schlägt er es nach, um seinen Wortschatz zu erweitern.
exercises.why: dazu introduces an additional action, and the final purpose clause is an um ... zu with the same subject.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why has the tram been rerouted? Because the rails are being repaired.
exercises.german: Weshalb wurde die Straßenbahn umgeleitet? Weil die Schienen repariert werden.
exercises.why: A weshalb-question expects a weil-answer; the passive in the answer keeps the finite verb were-werden with the participle last.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Save the file regularly so that you don't lose your work.
exercises.german: Speichere die Datei regelmäßig, um deine Arbeit nicht zu verlieren.
exercises.why: A negative purpose in which the negated object stands inside the um ... zu clause before the infinitive.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Leave a note so that nobody worries unnecessarily.
exercises.german: Lass einen Zettel da, damit sich niemand unnötig Sorgen macht.
exercises.why: A damit-clause with a reflexive verb and a negated subject, an idiom for final reassurance.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why did you hurry? Because I didn't want to miss my flight.
exercises.german: Warum bist du geeilt? Weil ich meinen Flug nicht verpassen wollte.
exercises.why: The weil-answer uses a modal in position II, which is what makes it formally a main clause and not a zu-clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: He signed up for the course in order not to lose his job.
exercises.german: Er hat sich für den Kurs angemeldet, um seinen Job nicht zu verlieren.
exercises.why: Separable verb anmelden in the perfect main clause; negative purpose with nicht inside the purpose clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: They are renovating the flat, and in addition they are installing new windows, in order to reduce the heating costs.
exercises.german: Sie renovieren die Wohnung, dazu bauen sie neue Fenster ein, um die Heizkosten zu senken.
exercises.why: dazu plus a second main clause before the um ... zu purpose clause; the subject sie governs all three parts.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why did you turn off the light? To save energy.
exercises.german: Warum hast du das Licht ausgemacht? Um Energie zu sparen.
exercises.why: A warum-question answered by a bare um ... zu infinitive without a conjugated verb or subject.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Hold on to the railing so that you don't fall.
exercises.german: Halte dich am Geländer fest, um nicht zu stürzen.
exercises.why: Negative purpose with the reflexive sich; the zu-infinitive of stürzen is the final word.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why are you copying the text? In order to study it later.
exercises.german: Wieso kopierst du den Text? Dazu, um ihn später zu lernen.
exercises.why: dazu, um ... zu expands a previously mentioned action with its purpose; that fixed phrase has no um alone.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: I watch the display board in order not to miss my stop.
exercises.german: Ich schaue auf die Anzeigetafel, um meine Haltestelle nicht zu verpassen.
exercises.why: The negated purpose is expressed with um nicht ... zu; verpassen is the zu-infinitive at the end of the sentence.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why has the deadline been moved? Because the data were incomplete.
exercises.german: Weshalb wurde die Frist verschoben? Weil die Daten unvollständig waren.
exercises.why: The passive in the question (wurde) is answered by a weil-clause whose preterite war goes last.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: I wear a scarf in order not to catch a cold.
exercises.german: Ich trage einen Schal, um keine Erkältung zu bekommen.
exercises.why: Negative purpose with a nominalised object (keine Erkältung); the same subject justifies um ... zu.

exercises.skill: Purpose extras: um nicht ... zu, dazu um ... zu, warum / wieso / weshalb questions
exercises.english: Why is the meeting being moved to Friday? To give the team more time to prepare.
exercises.german: Warum wird die Besprechung auf Freitag verlegt? Damit das Team mehr Zeit zur Vorbereitung hat.
exercises.why: A warum-question about a passive event is answered with damit, because the new subject is das Team.
